unit.title: Đọc B2
unit.summary: Giấc mơ, kinh tế gig, thành phố hay nông thôn, AI ở nơi làm việc, lối sống tối giản.

lessons.title: Vì sao ta mơ
lessons.summary: Các giả thuyết khoa học về giấc mơ.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Everybody dreams, although many people forget their dreams within minutes of waking up. Scientists have been studying dreams for over a century, yet they still disagree about why we dream at all.
paragraphs.vi: Ai cũng mơ, dù nhiều người quên giấc mơ chỉ vài phút sau khi thức. Các nhà khoa học nghiên cứu giấc mơ hơn một thế kỷ nhưng vẫn bất đồng về việc vì sao ta mơ.

paragraphs.en: One theory suggests that dreaming helps the brain process emotions and organise memories. Another argues that dreams are simply a by-product of random brain activity, which the mind then tries to turn into a story.
paragraphs.vi: Một giả thuyết cho rằng giấc mơ giúp não xử lý cảm xúc và sắp xếp ký ức. Giả thuyết khác lập luận giấc mơ chỉ là sản phẩm phụ của hoạt động ngẫu nhiên của não, rồi tâm trí cố biến nó thành câu chuyện.

paragraphs.en: Whatever the explanation, research shows that people who are deprived of dream-rich sleep tend to have more difficulty concentrating and controlling their mood. In other words, even if dreams have no meaning, the sleep that produces them is essential.
paragraphs.vi: Dù lý giải thế nào, nghiên cứu cho thấy người bị thiếu giấc ngủ nhiều mộng thường khó tập trung và kiểm soát tâm trạng hơn. Nói cách khác, dù giấc mơ không có ý nghĩa, giấc ngủ tạo ra chúng là thiết yếu.

headings: Two competing explanations for dreaming
Dreams as a source of creative ideas
A universal experience that science cannot yet explain
How to remember your dreams after waking
Why the sleep behind dreams matters either way
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: everybody dreams, but scientists still disagree about why; paragraph 2 sets out two theories; paragraph 3 argues that dream-rich sleep is essential whatever dreams mean. The passage says nothing about creativity or techniques for remembering dreams.

exercises.prompt: What is the writer's main conclusion?
choices: Dreams are simply random brain activity.
Whatever dreams mean, the sleep in which they occur matters a great deal.
Dreams mainly help us organise memories.
Scientists will soon discover why we dream.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "even if dreams have no meaning, the sleep that produces them is essential." The two theories in paragraph 2 are presented, not chosen between, and paragraph 1 says scientists still disagree.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "deprived" is closest in meaning to …
choices: given extra
warned about
prevented from having
cured by
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: people "deprived of dream-rich sleep" have trouble concentrating, so they are kept from getting that sleep — prevented from having it.

exercises.prompt: What does the second theory in paragraph 2 imply about the stories we experience in dreams?
choices: They are carefully planned by the brain to solve problems.
They help us control our mood.
They predict events in our future.
They may not carry any real meaning.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: dreams are "simply a by-product of random brain activity" which the mind turns into a story, so the story is built from noise and need not mean anything. "Random" rules out careful planning.

exercises.statement: Researchers now agree on the purpose of dreaming.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: after more than a century of study, scientists "still disagree about why we dream at all".

exercises.statement: It is common for people to forget a dream soon after waking.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: "many people forget their dreams within minutes of waking up".
The passage never compares children and adults.

exercises.prompt: Even if dreams have no meaning, the sleep is ___.
choices: essential
optional
short

exercises.text: Although everyone dreams, scientists still cannot ___ on the reason. Some think dreams help the brain handle feelings and sort ___, while others regard them as a side effect of ___ activity that the mind shapes into a narrative. Either way, people who lose dream-rich sleep find it harder to ___ and to manage their mood.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: scientists "still disagree"; paragraph 2: dreams may "organise memories" or be a by-product of "random brain activity"; paragraph 3: deprived people have "difficulty concentrating".

lessons.title: Kinh tế làm thuê tự do
lessons.summary: Làm việc theo từng đơn thay vì công việc cố định.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: In recent years, more people have started working "gigs": short-term jobs such as driving for a ride-hailing app, delivering food or doing freelance design. The internet has made it easy to find customers without an employer.
paragraphs.vi: Những năm gần đây, nhiều người bắt đầu làm "gig": công việc ngắn hạn như lái xe công nghệ, giao đồ ăn hay thiết kế tự do. Internet khiến việc tìm khách hàng không cần chủ thuê trở nên dễ dàng.

paragraphs.en: Supporters point out that gig work offers freedom: workers choose when and where to work, and they can earn extra money besides their main job. For students and parents with young children, this flexibility can be very valuable.
paragraphs.vi: Người ủng hộ chỉ ra rằng làm gig mang lại tự do: người làm chọn thời gian, địa điểm và kiếm thêm ngoài công việc chính. Với sinh viên và cha mẹ có con nhỏ, sự linh hoạt này rất quý.

paragraphs.en: Critics, however, warn that gig workers often lack benefits such as paid holidays, sick pay and pensions, and their income can change dramatically from month to month. They argue that regulation is necessary to protect workers without destroying the flexibility.
paragraphs.vi: Tuy nhiên những người phê phán cảnh báo người làm gig thường thiếu phúc lợi như nghỉ phép có lương, trợ cấp ốm đau, lương hưu và thu nhập có thể biến động mạnh theo tháng. Họ cho rằng cần quy định để bảo vệ người lao động mà không phá vỡ sự linh hoạt.

headings: The appeal of flexible work
How much gig workers earn
A new way of working made possible by technology
Why ride-hailing apps are so popular
Concerns about security and calls for rules
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 introduces gig work and credits the internet; paragraph 2 gives the supporters' case for freedom and flexibility; paragraph 3 gives the critics' worries and their call for regulation. Ride-hailing is only one example, and the passage gives no earnings figures.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best summarises the passage?
choices: Gig work is replacing all traditional jobs.
Gig work offers flexibility but raises concerns about workers' security.
Gig work should be banned because it is unfair.
Gig work is only suitable for students.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2 presents the freedom gig work offers; paragraph 3 presents the lack of benefits and unstable income. Even the critics want to keep the flexibility, so nobody calls for a ban.

exercises.prompt: Why does the writer mention students and parents with young children?
choices: To show that gig work is mostly done by young people
To argue that these groups need more regulation
To give examples of people for whom flexible hours are especially useful
To explain why gig workers lack sick pay
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "For students and parents with young children, this flexibility can be very valuable" — they illustrate who benefits most from choosing when to work.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 3, the word "dramatically" is closest in meaning to …
choices: slightly
greatly
regularly
slowly
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: income "can change dramatically from month to month" is listed as a serious risk, so the changes are large — greatly.

exercises.prompt: Which of the following would the critics in paragraph 3 most likely support?
choices: Banning ride-hailing apps completely
Leaving gig work without any rules
Forcing all gig workers to accept fixed working hours
Laws that give gig workers some benefits while keeping flexible hours
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: critics want regulation "to protect workers without destroying the flexibility". Fixed hours would destroy the flexibility, and no rules at all would not protect workers.

exercises.statement: Gig workers usually receive pensions from their employers.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: gig workers "often lack benefits such as paid holidays, sick pay and pensions"; paragraph 1 adds that they find customers without an employer.

exercises.statement: Supporters note that some people do gig work alongside a main job.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: workers "can earn extra money besides their main job".

exercises.statement: Most gig workers are under twenty.
exercises.explain: The passage mentions students as one group who value flexibility but gives no information about the age of most gig workers.

exercises.text: With the help of the internet, many people now take on short-term ___ without working for a single employer. Supporters value the ___ to choose their own hours and place of work. Critics, however, point out that gig workers often have no paid leave or sick pay and that their ___ can vary widely. They call for ___ that protects workers without removing the flexibility.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: gigs are "short-term jobs"; paragraph 2: gig work "offers freedom"; paragraph 3: "their income can change dramatically" and critics argue "regulation is necessary".

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: The debate between city and countryside living is as old as cities themselves. City dwellers enjoy a wide choice of jobs, restaurants and entertainment, while people in the countryside value space, clean air and a stronger sense of community.
paragraphs.vi: Cuộc tranh luận giữa sống ở thành phố và nông thôn cũng cũ như chính các thành phố. Dân thành thị hưởng nhiều lựa chọn về việc làm, nhà hàng, giải trí, còn người nông thôn coi trọng không gian, không khí sạch và tinh thần cộng đồng bền chặt hơn.

paragraphs.en: On the other hand, cities are often noisy, crowded and expensive, and many residents spend hours commuting. In rural areas, public services such as hospitals, schools and transport may be far away, and young people sometimes find fewer opportunities.
paragraphs.vi: Mặt khác, thành phố thường ồn ào, đông đúc, đắt đỏ và nhiều cư dân mất hàng giờ đi lại. Ở nông thôn, các dịch vụ công như bệnh viện, trường học, giao thông có thể ở xa và giới trẻ đôi khi thấy ít cơ hội hơn.

paragraphs.en: Thanks to remote work and better internet, a growing number of people are moving out of big cities without giving up their careers. Perhaps the best choice depends less on location and more on what each person values most.
paragraphs.vi: Nhờ làm việc từ xa và Internet tốt hơn, ngày càng nhiều người rời thành phố lớn mà không bỏ sự nghiệp. Có lẽ lựa chọn tốt nhất ít phụ thuộc vào nơi ở mà phụ thuộc vào điều mỗi người coi trọng nhất.

headings: The downsides of both ways of life
A shortage of hospitals in villages
What each way of life has to offer
The rising cost of rural housing
New possibilities and a personal decision
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 lists what cities and the countryside each offer; paragraph 2 ("On the other hand") lists the drawbacks of both; paragraph 3 describes remote work and concludes that the choice depends on personal values. Distant hospitals are only one detail of paragraph 2, and rural housing costs are not mentioned.

exercises.prompt: What is the writer's overall view?
choices: City life is clearly better because of job opportunities.
Everyone should move to the countryside to escape noise.
There is no single best choice; it depends on personal priorities.
Remote work will soon empty big cities.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "the best choice depends less on location and more on what each person values most". The writer gives both sides fairly and predicts no mass exodus.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 1, the word "dwellers" is closest in meaning to …
choices: residents
visitors
workers
builders
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: "City dwellers" are contrasted with "people in the countryside", so dwellers are the people who live there — residents.

exercises.prompt: What does paragraph 3 suggest was often true before remote work became common?
choices: Rural areas had better internet than cities.
Few people worked in cities.
Remote work was more common than it is now.
Leaving a big city often meant giving up one's career.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: thanks to remote work, people can now move out "without giving up their careers", which implies that moving out used to cost many people their careers. Better internet is presented as new.

exercises.statement: Long journeys to work are a problem for many people in cities.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "many residents spend hours commuting".

exercises.statement: The passage claims that young people in rural areas always have plenty of opportunities.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: in rural areas "young people sometimes find fewer opportunities".

exercises.statement: The writer lives in the countryside.
exercises.explain: The passage compares both ways of life but never says where the writer lives.

exercises.prompt: The best choice depends on what each person ___ most.
choices: values
buys
hears

exercises.text: People have long argued about whether cities or the countryside offer a better life. Cities provide plenty of jobs and ___, while rural areas offer space, fresh air and a close ___. Yet cities can be noisy and costly, and in the countryside, services such as hospitals may be ___. Now that many people can work ___, more of them are leaving big cities.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: cities offer jobs, restaurants and "entertainment"; the countryside offers "a stronger sense of community"; paragraph 2: public services "may be far away"; paragraph 3: "remote work" lets people leave cities.

lessons.title: Trí tuệ nhân tạo ở nơi làm việc
lessons.summary: AI thay đổi công việc thế nào.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Artificial intelligence is no longer a technology of the future; it already helps doctors read scans, banks detect fraud and teachers prepare materials. Many routine tasks that once took hours can now be completed in minutes.
paragraphs.vi: Trí tuệ nhân tạo không còn là công nghệ của tương lai; nó đã giúp bác sĩ đọc phim chụp, ngân hàng phát hiện gian lận và giáo viên soạn tài liệu. Nhiều việc thường nhật từng mất hàng giờ nay hoàn thành trong vài phút.

paragraphs.en: This progress raises an important question: will machines replace human workers? Most economists believe that some jobs will disappear, but new ones will emerge, as happened with earlier technologies. What matters is whether workers have the chance to learn new skills.
paragraphs.vi: Tiến bộ này đặt ra câu hỏi quan trọng: máy móc có thay thế người lao động không? Hầu hết nhà kinh tế tin một số việc sẽ biến mất nhưng việc mới sẽ xuất hiện như đã xảy ra với các công nghệ trước. Điều quan trọng là người lao động có cơ hội học kỹ năng mới hay không.

paragraphs.en: In practice, the most effective approach seems to be collaboration: AI handles repetitive work and large amounts of data, while people contribute judgement, creativity and empathy. Employees who learn to use these tools wisely are likely to become more valuable, not less.
paragraphs.vi: Trên thực tế, cách hiệu quả nhất có vẻ là hợp tác: AI xử lý việc lặp lại và lượng dữ liệu lớn, còn con người đóng góp sự phán đoán, sáng tạo và đồng cảm. Nhân viên biết dùng các công cụ này khôn ngoan nhiều khả năng sẽ có giá trị hơn chứ không kém đi.

headings: How AI detects bank fraud
Humans and machines working side by side
Why AI will never make mistakes
A technology already in everyday use
Job losses, job gains and the need to retrain
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: AI is "no longer a technology of the future" and already helps many professions; paragraph 2: some jobs disappear, new ones emerge, and learning new skills matters; paragraph 3: collaboration between AI and people. Fraud detection is only one example, and the passage never claims AI is error-free.

exercises.prompt: Which statement best expresses the writer's position?
choices: AI will soon replace most human workers.
AI works best when it supports people rather than replaces them.
Workers should avoid AI to protect their jobs.
AI is still a technology of the distant future.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "the most effective approach seems to be collaboration", and employees who use AI wisely become "more valuable, not less". Paragraph 1 says AI is already here, not in the future.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "emerge" is closest in meaning to …
choices: vanish
decline
appear
combine
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "some jobs will disappear, but new ones will emerge" — the contrast with "disappear" shows that emerge means come into existence, appear.

exercises.prompt: What does the reference to "earlier technologies" in paragraph 2 suggest?
choices: Earlier technologies created no new jobs.
AI is less powerful than earlier technologies.
Economists were wrong about earlier technologies.
New technologies have tended to change jobs rather than simply destroy them.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: new jobs will emerge "as happened with earlier technologies", so history shows jobs being lost and created, not just destroyed.

exercises.prompt: Based on paragraph 2, which workers are likely to face the greatest risk?
choices: Those who have no opportunity to learn new skills
Doctors who use AI to read scans
Employees who use AI tools wisely
Economists who study technology
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "What matters is whether workers have the chance to learn new skills", so those without that chance are most exposed. Paragraph 3 says employees who use AI wisely become more valuable.

exercises.statement: The passage mentions uses of AI in healthcare, finance and education.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: AI helps "doctors read scans, banks detect fraud and teachers prepare materials".

exercises.statement: The writer thinks workers should avoid AI tools.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: employees who learn to use these tools wisely "are likely to become more valuable, not less".

exercises.statement: AI will be cheaper than teachers within five years.
exercises.explain: The passage says AI helps teachers prepare materials but says nothing about cost or a five-year timescale.

exercises.prompt: AI handles repetitive work and large amounts of ___.
choices: data
coffee
music

exercises.text: AI is already common at work, completing ___ tasks much faster than people once could. Economists expect some jobs to vanish and others to be ___, so the real issue is whether workers get the chance to learn new ___. The most effective model is a partnership in which machines take on repetitive work while humans contribute ___, imagination and understanding of others.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: "routine tasks" now take minutes; paragraph 2: new jobs "will emerge" and workers need to "learn new skills"; paragraph 3: people contribute "judgement, creativity and empathy".

lessons.title: Lối sống tối giản
lessons.summary: Sống với ít đồ hơn để có nhiều thời gian hơn.

blocks.md: Đọc một lượt lấy ý chính, bấm vào từ lạ để tra, rồi mới làm câu hỏi. Từ nào khó hơn trình độ của bạn sẽ được gạch chấm.

paragraphs.en: Minimalism is the idea that owning fewer things can lead to a happier and less stressful life. Rather than buying more, followers of this lifestyle ask themselves whether each item really adds value to their lives.
paragraphs.vi: Chủ nghĩa tối giản là ý tưởng rằng sở hữu ít đồ hơn có thể dẫn đến cuộc sống hạnh phúc, ít căng thẳng hơn. Thay vì mua thêm, người theo lối sống này tự hỏi từng món đồ có thật sự thêm giá trị cho cuộc sống hay không.

paragraphs.en: The benefits can be considerable. People who simplify their homes often report saving money, spending less time cleaning and feeling more in control. They also tend to have more time for relationships and experiences instead of possessions.
paragraphs.vi: Lợi ích có thể đáng kể. Người đơn giản hoá nhà cửa thường kể rằng họ tiết kiệm tiền, mất ít thời gian dọn dẹp hơn và thấy chủ động hơn. Họ cũng thường có nhiều thời gian hơn cho các mối quan hệ và trải nghiệm thay vì đồ đạc.

paragraphs.en: Critics argue that extreme minimalism can be a privilege, since not everyone can afford to throw things away and replace them later. A more realistic approach is simply to buy thoughtfully, repair what you can, and keep only what you use or love.
paragraphs.vi: Người phê phán cho rằng tối giản cực đoan có thể là đặc quyền vì không phải ai cũng đủ khả năng vứt đồ rồi mua lại sau. Cách thực tế hơn là chỉ mua có suy nghĩ, sửa những gì có thể và giữ lại những gì bạn dùng hoặc yêu thích.

headings: Why minimalists dislike cleaning
What people gain from simplifying
The environmental cost of shopping
The basic principle behind owning less
A criticism and a more balanced approach
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1 defines minimalism; paragraph 2 lists its benefits; paragraph 3 gives the critics' view and a more realistic approach. Less cleaning is only one benefit, and the passage never discusses the environment.

exercises.prompt: What is the main purpose of paragraph 3?
choices: To question an extreme form of minimalism and suggest a moderate alternative
To list the financial benefits of minimalism
To explain how minimalism began
To encourage readers to throw away most of their belongings
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: critics call "extreme minimalism" a privilege, and the writer then offers "a more realistic approach": buy thoughtfully, repair and keep what you use or love.

exercises.prompt: In paragraph 2, the word "considerable" is closest in meaning to …
choices: minor
unexpected
significant
temporary
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: "The benefits can be considerable", followed by a list of savings, time and control, so the benefits are large — significant.

exercises.prompt: Which person's behaviour best matches the "more realistic approach" in paragraph 3?
choices: Someone who throws away anything not used in the past week
Someone who keeps every gift they have ever received
Someone who often buys cheap items and replaces them
Someone who fixes a broken chair instead of buying a new one
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: the realistic approach is to "buy thoughtfully, repair what you can, and keep only what you use or love". Fixing a chair is repairing; keeping everything or replacing items often goes against it.

exercises.prompt: According to the critics, why is extreme minimalism not an option for everyone?
choices: Most people enjoy shopping too much.
Not everyone can afford to discard things and buy them again later.
Small homes are hard to find.
It takes too much time to clean.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: "not everyone can afford to throw things away and replace them later", which is why critics call it a privilege.

exercises.statement: People who own fewer things tend to have more time for other people.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 2: they "tend to have more time for relationships and experiences instead of possessions".

exercises.statement: Everyone can easily afford extreme minimalism.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 3: critics say extreme minimalism "can be a privilege, since not everyone can afford" it.
The passage does not say where or when minimalism began.

exercises.text: Minimalism is based on the belief that having fewer ___ can reduce stress. Its followers often save money and feel more in ___ of their lives. Critics, however, note that only people with enough money can easily discard items and ___ them later. A sensible middle path is to shop carefully, ___ broken things and keep only what is truly useful or loved.
exercises.explain: Paragraph 1: "owning fewer things"; paragraph 2: people feel "more in control"; paragraph 3: not everyone can "throw things away and replace them later", and the realistic approach is to "repair what you can".
